transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Herbst.
President Trump continues a series of rallies to support Republican candidates heading into
the midterm elections, with a rally in Ohio tonight.
For member station WYSO, Jerry Kenney has more.
The president isn't scheduled to speak until 7 o'clock tonight, but the crowd is already
gathering at Vandalia Butler High School.
Trump is stumping for the incumbent Republican Senate candidate John Husted, who's in a
tight race with former Ohio Senator Sherrod Brown.
Husted was appointed by Governor Mike DeWine to fill Vice President J.D. Vance's Senate
seat in 2025.
The president is sure to tout his economic accomplishments tonight, but with low approval
ratings and many Americans still reeling from high gas prices and other economic struggles,
it's unclear if his message will resonate with voters and help carry Husted over the
finish line in November.
For NPR News, I'm Jerry Kenney in Yellow Springs.
There are new details in the investigation in the mid-air attack on board a commercial
plane from Dubai to Tel Aviv earlier this week.
NPR's Kat Lonsdorf reports the United Arab Emirates, which is leading the probe, has
deemed the incident an attempted terrorist attack.
Investigators in the UAE announced that the Fly Dubai co-pilot, who carried out the attack
mid-flight, assaulted the captain of the plane using what's called a crash axe, a lightweight
emergency tool stored in the cockpit to break through panels or jam doors in the event of
a crash.
Investigators said the attacker then tried to seize control of the plane's flight mechanisms.
The plane had 174 people on board, many of whom are Israeli.
Israeli officials had already deemed it an attempted terrorist attack.
Saudi investigators have now agreed.
Both the pilot and co-pilot are live and being questioned, and the investigation is ongoing.
Israel has said the attacker is from Oman, although that has yet to be confirmed by Emirati,
Saudi, or Omani officials.
Kat Lonsdorf, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
The Food and Drug Administration has closed its investigation into this year's cyclospora
outbreak, the largest on record in the U.S.
NPR's Matt Bloom has more.
In the update, the FDA confirmed its inspectors found the parasite in two places in Mexico,
a drainage ditch at an iceberg lettuce farm used as an independent grower for Taylor Farms
and inside a wastewater tank at their processing facility.
It remains unclear exactly how the contamination took place, but the agency says the evidence
supports a strong link between the lettuce and nearly 13,000 cases.
Taylor Farms blamed the contamination on an independent grower it says is no longer a
part of its supply chain.
The FDA says it will now continue some response activities to help prevent future outbreaks.
Matt Bloom, NPR News.
And the FDA says more than 12,000 confirmed U.S. cases were tied to the recalled lettuce.
This is NPR News.
RM, the K-pop idol and leader of the globetrotting boy band BTS, has turned museum curator.
And if here's Chloe Veltman reports, a new exhibition opening today at the San Francisco
Museum of Modern Art is the first ever to feature the South Korean Superstars art collection.
The exhibition includes well over a hundred works from RM's collection.
It highlights ancient and contemporary Korean paintings, objects and sculptures, including
works by some of RM's favourite artists like Kim Won-ki and Yeon Hyung-kyun.
At a press briefing for the show, the self-deprecating musician said he loves collecting art, but
also feels guilty about it.
Do I really need to carry so many unnecessary things that I don't even need?
Have I ended up becoming just a boring rich snore?
Well maybe.
RM started collecting art in 2019.
He sings about his passion on tracks like still life.
Chloe Veltman, NPR News.
It's not just rising gas and diesel prices that are causing Americans financial headaches.
Jet fuel is also on the rise.
The average price rose to $4.39 a gallon a record.
Industry trade group Airlines for America says that has airlines cutting flights and
retiring older aircraft to keep the costs down.
But as the holiday traveling season nears, it also means passengers are paying more for
their tickets.
Travel website kayaks says the average domestic fare rose more than $400, the highest this
year.
I'm Janine Herbst, NPR News, in Washington.

topics.text: President Trump holds rally in Ohio to support Republican Senate candidate John Husted
Fly Dubai co-pilot attacks captain with crash axe in mid-air incident from Dubai to Tel Aviv
FDA closes investigation into record cyclospora outbreak linked to Taylor Farms lettuce in Mexico
BTS leader RM curates first-ever exhibition of his art collection at San Francisco Museum of Modern Art
Rising jet fuel prices prompt airlines to cut flights and increase ticket fares for passengers
